outcome: massive transfusion (transfusion of more than eight units of red blood cells on the day of childbirth)
cohort: The study included 294,695 women who had undergone elective cesarean section from January 2013 to August 2018, based on inpatient medical records from tertiary hospitals in mainland China.
finding: Ten specific antepartum risk factors were identified to be associated with massive transfusion in women undergoing elective cesarean section, with placenta previa and coagulopathy showing the strongest associations.
mod_finding: The study focused specifically on elective cesarean sections, noting that risk factors for massive transfusion might differ by mode of birth, but did not compare findings across different modes.
